There are basically two definitions of cultural appropriation, one of which is at least partially sane and the other of which is not.

The more sane version centers around a situation where a (typically more powerful/dominant) culture adopts and trivializes cultural elements of another that are of particular significance. Usually these things are religious or ceremonial, but more generally they signify great respect or position. Maori facial tattoos, Native headdresses, the Pope's hat, we're talking about things that (and this is important) must a) be earned in some way, b) are heavily restricted even inside the relevant culture and c) have historically been granted by an identifiable authority like a religious or tribal council. Needless to say, people get pissed off when they see some random at a concert wearing and making a mess of something that, to them, is a Really Big Deal - it's similar to people freaking out because someone burned (or shit on, rolled joints out of, generally defaced, etc.) a bible or koran or torah, stuck a crucifix in a bottle of urine and called it art....and so on. For most intents and purposes, here we're talking about things that could reasonably and meaningfully be called "cultural trademarks," are a big deal to those involved, and are genuinely tied to the culture. As an atheist without much of an identifiable cultural background it's hard for me to understand on an intuitive level, but at least intellectually I can sympathize with someone getting bent out of shape when they see drunken idiots making a mockery of something in that way.

I don't believe there's a truly "good" solution to the problem, but existing IP (i.e. trademark and copyright) law makes a surprisingly good start - even if the general idea (i.e. headdresses) can't be limited, there's no reason that the specific designs can't be restricted and given legal status (i.e. giving indefinite copyright to a tribal authority if one exists). Even then, things get complicated when one group cares and another doesn't or even wants to exploit it for profit, but it's better than nothing.

The other version is what happens when we drop the a), b) and c) from the first one. Suddenly, "appropriation" becomes "any time a group we don't like uses something general that I think 'we' invented." Dreadlocks, general items of clothing, musical styles....the list goes on. People have a problem with it because they feel (or want to feel) a sense of ownership over the concept or category, which becomes hard to do when another (larger) culture starts using it. Instead of people getting (at least somewhat) reasonably pissed over people basically mocking their central cultural traditions, it's a lot more like hipsters bitching at the mainstream for "ruining" something by mass-producing it. In some cases this may actually involve some legitimate gripes (i.e. mass-production can make a mess of things and make it a pain in the ass to find the "original" version if that's what you're looking for), but for the most part it's just people looking for something to be offended and feel morally superior about.
